quick: No change in mild-moderate; not studied in severe
Limit; may worsen hot flushes/bone loss
Bone mineral density, cholesterol, cardiac status
summary: Anastrozole is a selective non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor for postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer: adjuvant treatment of early disease, first-line for advanced/metastatic disease, and second-line after tamoxifen. It lowers estradiol by blocking peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogens. Dose is 1 mg once daily. Key risks are reduced bone mineral density, raised cholesterol, ischemic cardiac events in women with pre-existing heart disease, and fetal harm.
indications: Adjuvant treatment of postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer
First-line treatment of postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive or unknown locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
Treatment of advanced breast cancer in postmenopausal women with disease progression following tamoxifen therapy

dosage.n: Typically ~5 years (per ATAC); optimal duration individualized
Not studied in severe hepatic impairment

admin: Take one 1 mg tablet once daily, with or without food
Confirm postmenopausal status; verify pregnancy status before starting in women of reproductive potential
May be taken at any consistent time of day
For advanced disease, continue until disease progression
Counsel on bone health (calcium, vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise)
moa: Growth of many breast cancers is driven by estrogens. In postmenopausal women, estrogens come mainly from aromatase-mediated conversion of adrenal androgens (androstenedione, testosterone) to estrone and estradiol in peripheral tissues. Anastrozole is a selective non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor that markedly lowers serum estradiol without detectable effect on adrenal corticosteroid or aldosterone production, reducing estrogen-dependent tumor growth.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to anastrozole or any excipient (anaphylaxis, angioedema, urticaria)
monitor: Cardiac status in women with ischemic heart disease

preg: Contraindicated - based on animal data and mechanism, anastrozole may cause fetal harm. Verify pregnancy status before starting and advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception (the indicated population is postmenopausal women).
lact: Do not breastfeed during treatment with anastrozole.
renal: No dosage adjustment is necessary in renal impairment.
hepatic: No dose change for mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment. Anastrozole has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment - use caution.

major: Tamoxifen / estrogen-containing therapies - reduce anastrozole plasma levels and may antagonize its effect; do not co-administer
moderate: Other estrogens - counteract the pharmacologic action of anastrozole
minor: Drugs affecting bone metabolism - additive effect on BMD
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no clinically significant food interaction.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; it can worsen hot flushes and contribute to bone loss.
interactions.diagnostics: Lowers serum estradiol; may raise total cholesterol/LDL and liver enzymes; may reduce bone mineral density.

serious: Ischemic cardiovascular events (in women with pre-existing ischemic heart disease)
rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome and other severe skin reactions

monitoring: Cardiac assessment in women with ischemic heart disease
Liver function if symptoms suggest hepatotoxicity
counsel: Take one tablet daily at about the same time; it can be taken with or without food
Joint aches and hot flushes are common - report if severe or limiting
Look after your bones: calcium, vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise; bone density will be checked
Report chest pain or breathlessness, or signs of an allergic reaction (swelling, rash, difficulty breathing)
Do not take with tamoxifen or estrogen products; tell your doctor about all medicines
pk: Estradiol suppression within ~24 h of dosing
Plasma peak ~2 h fasting; steady state in ~7 days
Store at 20-25 C; preserve in a tight container
pearls: For POSTMENOPAUSAL women only with hormone receptor-positive disease
Bone loss is a key long-term effect - monitor BMD and support bone health
Increased ischemic cardiac events in women with pre-existing ischemic heart disease - weigh risk/benefit
Do not combine with tamoxifen or estrogens (reduced efficacy)
Joint/musculoskeletal symptoms are common and a frequent cause of non-adherence
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose - do not take two tablets at once.
overdose: No specific antidote; clinical experience with overdose is limited. Manage with supportive care. As anastrozole is not highly protein bound, dialysis may help; treat symptomatically.
